programme: SMAD7, the inhibitory SMAD that terminates TGF-β/BMP receptor signalling, paired with HDAC3 as its transcriptional corepressor — HDAC3 targets SMAD7 directly in this network, matching the documented SMAD7-HDAC1/3-SIN3A complex that represses TGF-β target genes and helps degrade the receptor complex.
role_in_a: In Lower_Grade_Glioma, TGF-β/SMAD signalling drives invasiveness and immune modulation; two studies show TGF-β-induced miRNAs (miR-132; miR-205/miR-195) actively suppressing SMAD7 to sustain pathway output, and HDAC3 expression maps onto patient survival, consistent with the corepressor arm reinforcing this circuit as tumours progress.
role_in_b: In Stroke, the same TGF-β/SMAD7 brake is engaged in the post-ischaemic reparative and neuroinflammatory response: an electroacupuncture study shows the miR-21-5p/TGF-β/SMAD axis modulating post-stroke pain, while separate work targets HDAC (including HDAC3) pharmacologically to reprogram microglia and blunt oxidative stress after cerebral ischaemia — i.e. the corepressor arm is being manipulated therapeutically in stroke models.
shared_axis: A slow-growing tumour and an acute ischaemic injury both recruit the TGF-β/SMAD7 repair circuit for opposite ends — stromal/immune remodelling for the former, control of post-injury inflammation and glial repair for the latter — so the SMAD7-HDAC3 brake on that pathway resurfaces as a control point in both tissues without the diseases otherwise being related.
reasoning: SMAD7 and HDAC3 are the only two of the twelve listed factors with direct, disease-specific citations in both diseases, and the network's own HDAC3→SMAD7 edge matches known corepressor biology, so the module is nameable and independently placed in each disease. But no retrieved paper puts Lower_Grade_Glioma and Stroke together through this axis, and several citations are model-specific or interventional (rat electroacupuncture, HDAC-inhibitor nanoparticle delivery) rather than clean endogenous characterisation, so the cross-disease bridge itself is inferential.
support: PMID 25791281 (HDAC3 expression mapped and linked to survival in Lower_Grade_Glioma); PMID 25983322 (TGF-β/miR-132 represses SMAD7, sustaining TGF-β signalling in a glioma-relevant system); PMID 27574009 (TGF-β1/miR-205/miR-195 target SMAD7 within the TGF-β pathway, glioma-linked); PMID 41454256 (electroacupuncture modulates miR-21-5p/TGF-β/SMAD7 signalling in a rat post-stroke pain model); PMID 42677156 (HDAC-targeted pH-responsive nanoparticle delivery modulates microglial neuroinflammation in stroke models); PMID 42517197 (melatonin plus the HDAC inhibitor valproic acid modulate oxidative stress in cerebral ischaemia).
how_to_falsify: In parallel glioma cell-line and rodent MCAO ischaemia systems, use ChIP and co-IP to test whether HDAC3 occupies and represses the SMAD7 locus and whether SMAD7-HDAC3 complex formation tracks with repression of TGF-β target genes; if HDAC3 does not bind or regulate SMAD7 in one or both systems, or TGF-β target derepression does not follow HDAC3 loss, the shared-module account fails.
caveats: blood|brain tissue pairing over 93 patient-group comparisons from 4 independent cohort pairs; recurrence fractions (55/93 for HDAC3, 46/93 for SMAD7) describe how often the edge reappeared, not per-comparison significance. NOTCH1, the exclusion list's highest-recurrence factor (0.52) and a canonical driver in both glioma and cerebrovascular biology, was removed as tissue-generic and must not be reintroduced to strengthen this story. Ten of the twelve listed factors (POU4F2, MEIS1, SOX17, ZNF281, HSF4, ETV1, AHRR, TBPL1, TCFL5, GTF3A) have no disease-specific literature support in the record and are not part of this account, so the module covers only 2 of 12 factors, not the full list.
